finding.claim: SQL injection through object keys. With `permitSetMultiParamEntries` enabled, a plain-object parameter is expanded into `` `key`=value `` pairs. The key is wrapped in backticks without escaping embedded backticks, so a key such as ``a`=1, `admin`=1 -- `` breaks out of the identifier and injects SQL. Only the values are escaped. The same flaw exists in the pre-escaped path in lib/misc/utils.js:213, used by `connection.escape` and `pool.escape`. The library's own `escapeId` (utils.js:106) doubles backticks, but this code does not use it. This is opt-in. An application is exposed only if it enables `permitSetMultiParamEntries` and passes a user-controlled object, for example a parsed JSON request body, as `SET ?` or `INSERT ... SET ?`.
finding.source: Keys of an object passed as a query parameter (for example `req.body` parsed from JSON), when the application sets `permitSetMultiParamEntries: true`.
finding.sink: SQL text sent to the server by the text protocol. out.writeString('`' + key + '`') at text-encoder.js:135, and the string concatenation at utils.js:213.

trace.note: Branch is taken only when permitSetMultiParamEntries is set and the object is not GeoJSON.
`for (let key in value)` iterates attacker-controlled keys.
The key is written raw between backticks with no doubling of backticks. Values go through writeParam, which is escaped.
Client-side escape path has the same iteration.
`'`' + key + '`='` is concatenated with no escaping. The sibling escapeId at utils.js:106 does escape backticks.

finding.guards_checked: The escaping applied to values (escapeString and writeStringEscapeQuote) covers only the right-hand side. There is no key validation, no escapeId call, and no allowlist on the path. The only gate is the opt-in option, and its default is off. I also checked the geo encoders (isNaN guards on coordinates), `escapeId` (doubles backticks and rejects NUL), the `USE` statement at connection.js:1442 (doubles backticks), LOCAL INFILE (parse.js:388 escapes regex metacharacters and the file name is checked against the client's own query), and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES handling in the string and buffer escapers. These are all enforced and I treated them as SAFE.
